gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Notebookcheck measured its 'best overall' pick, the UGREEN DXP6800 Pro, at 36.6–41.9 W idle with four HDDs. That is about 13–18 W more than the 4-bay boxes: 23.8 W for the TerraMaster F4-424 Pro (Notebookcheck) and 24.25 W for the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus on 2.5GbE (KitGuru). Running 24/7, that is roughly 115–160 kWh a year more.
standout_why: I read both pages ChatGPT cited. NASCompares' 'Terramaster F4-424 Pro – Should You Buy?' has no measured figures, only the CPU's 7 W TDP rating. NeedToKnowIT's 'TrueNAS and Unraid on UGREEN DXP' (updated 2026-10-04) has no watt, dB or throughput figures. The Notebookcheck F4-424 Pro review (rank 7, not cited) does carry the F4-424 Pro's 23.8 W idle and 33.7 dB idle. No result has the DXP6800 Pro or DXP4800 Plus measurements, and none puts the candidates side by side. The power and noise measurements are new. Only the F4-424 Pro baseline was already in ChatGPT's results.
decides: For an always-on Unraid/TrueNAS box, this supports our 4-bay picks (DXP4800 Plus, F4-424 Pro) over ChatGPT's DXP6800 Pro as the default. The 6-bay i5 box costs about 13–18 W more at idle in Notebookcheck's test. It only pays off if you need the bays or the CPU. KitGuru's figures also show the 10GbE link costs about 6 W at idle on the DXP4800 Plus (24.25 W vs 30.45 W), which a 2.5GbE-only buyer can avoid. The comparison is not like-for-like: drives and labs differ. It supports the pick but doesn't decide it alone.

findings.label: Power under Unraid (named forum owners)
findings.value: about 23–25 W with HDDs spun down (foo_fighter); about 30 W spun down, 41–45 W under load (Wura)
findings.source_title: Optimizing UGREEN DXP 4800 Plus on Unraid – Unraid forums
findings.note: Both posts 2024-11-23. foo_fighter read the figure off a UPS, with an SSD and a Coral USB running Frigate, after `powertop --auto` and Unraid's 'best efficiency' power mode, with the 10G NIC disabled in BIOS. Wura used only the AutoFan plugin, disk count not stated. These are owner measurements, not lab figures. They're the only figures I found for this box under a third-party OS.

findings.label: Idle and active power, four 22 TB HDDs (NASCompares)
findings.value: about 24.6 W idle, about 53.3 W active (averages)
findings.source_title: How Much Does it Cost to Run a NAS 24×7? QNAP & WD – NASCompares
findings.note: Rob Andrews, 2022. Four WD Red Pro 22 TB (WD221KFGX) in RAID 5, measured with a GOSUND smart plug. The article gives 24-hour totals of 0.59 and 1.28, labelled 'kW' but meaning kWh. Averages: 0.59/24 = 24.6 W, 1.28/24 = 53.3 W.
